answer: Identity is minted as hardware, not paperwork. At join, the local kernel seals a voting key to a fused per-chip secret, and the enclave signs an attestation quote binding that key to the device serial plus one slow memory-hard puzzle, so a single chip yields exactly one key. An attacker can rent a garden of virtual machines, but hypervisors cannot fabricate fused secrets, so every extra identity needs a distinct physical device whose velvet resale margin never covers the join cost.
